what: Thomson Reuters sells professional information and software. Westlaw is the research system used by American lawyers, Checkpoint by accountants, and it also supplies tax software, government compliance tools and the Reuters news agency.
customers: Law firms, corporate legal departments, accounting firms, tax professionals, governments and news organisations.
money: Westlaw research and legal workflow software
tax, legal and trade compliance software for companies
moat: Research systems lawyers and accountants are trained on, with proprietary editorial content built over a century that cannot be recreated from public sources.
risks: Artificial intelligence could let competitors build research tools more cheaply
Legal and accounting firm headcount drives seat-based pricing
Revenue grew only about 3% last year
Reuters News is a small and structurally difficult business
opportunities: Analysts see about 26% upside from current levels
Its own AI research assistants let it charge more per seat
Recurring subscription revenue is around 80% of the total
watch: Organic revenue growth in Legal Professionals and the uptake of its AI products.
